correctness.rationale: The cyclic-subgroup decomposition gives one common order-q clique and, for each of t p-lines, an order-p clique joined to an order-pq generator clique; only the latter meets the common q clique. True-twin obstruction allows at most one white per class, and force analysis proves that at most one branch may have both local classes white. Counting these profiles yields the polynomial. A t+2-dimensional indefinite Gram representation realizes the exact edge pattern; with M<=Z, exact minimum rank follows. The verifier exhausts all representative profiles for two parameter choices and reconstructs direct group graphs.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the full propagation enumerator, every minimum-set type, maximum nullity, and real minimum rank on a natural infinite algebraic family. Its global deadlock condition is stronger than a routine twin-class count and supplies a useful benchmark for more complicated nilpotent proper-power graphs.
